prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of the incretin hormone GLP-1 and the identity of its active peptide form, which made possible incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange my configuration is unchanged: a single-achievement B027 prize crediting Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The round-1 record shows that all six of us converged on the same trio, and the chair has rightly warned that this agreement could hide different readings of what is being honoured. So I state my reading explicitly. The achievement is the physiology of GLP-1: Holst's work on the incretin effect and GLP-1 secretion, Mojsov's identification of the biologically active truncated peptide forms, and Drucker's work on receptor action and the wider proglucagon-derived biology. That body of work defined a molecule and a receptor that could be targeted, and it is what the drug programmes were built on. Its consequences have been tested in large independent randomized trials, now covering glycaemia, weight, and cardiovascular and renal outcomes, and the interpretation has been stable for decades. This is the discernible change in a field that a discovery prize should recognise, and no other shortlisted candidate combines original mechanism with an equally complete and verified consequence for patients. I do not think a second part adds anything, because it would require cutting the B027 trio to two names, and the physiology chain is not divisible without losing a documented contributor.
statement.case_against: The attribution objection is real and I cannot dissolve it from the supplied material. Mojsov's priority for the active peptide relative to Habener's group, which is outside the credit list, is something I know only from recalled history and have not verified. Knudsen's engineering of long-acting analogues is what reached patients at scale, so a physiology-centred citation will be read by some as honouring the hormone but not the medicine. Equally, a therapy-centred citation would drift toward drug development and away from the discovery. There is also the risk that the Committee is moved by the public prominence of semaglutide and tirzepatide, which is not the same as scientific originality. I regard these as limits on the configuration, not reasons to abandon it, because the alternatives on the shortlist each carry an attribution or maturity problem that is at least as large.

responses.point: The chair asked whether the Committee honours GLP-1 physiology and molecular identity or incretin-based therapy, and whether any evidence in the supplied material can settle Mojsov's priority against Habener; the chair also moved from a Knudsen trio to the physiology trio after hearing colleagues.
responses.response: I answer the first question as physiology and molecular identity, with the citation saying that the discovery made the therapies possible, so that the drug-development step is acknowledged in the wording and not credited by a name. On the second question, nothing in the supplied material lets me settle Mojsov against Habener, and I will not pretend that it does. What I can say is that the structure of my argument does not depend on her being first. The discovery needs a named contributor for the identity of the active peptide, and if the Committee concluded from evidence that her contribution is not separable from Habener's, the right response is to reopen that seat for a considered decision, not to substitute Knudsen by default. I also note that the chair's move toward this trio is disclosed as influenced by us, and mine is likewise partly shaped by hearing the same argument repeated, so I have tried to test it and not merely accept it. I remain on Mojsov over Knudsen.

responses.point: Sandberg proposed B020 or B043 as the fallback and argued that B043 has the cleaner credit and maturity, while warning that the Committee risks rewarding an exceptionally visible clinical story at the expense of older, cleaner mechanistic discoveries.
responses.response: The warning is fair and I have tried to apply it to myself. The test I used is whether B027 would still be first if semaglutide and tirzepatide had never become household names, and I think it would, because the physiology chain stands on Holst, Mojsov and Drucker and on the outcome trials, not on commercial success. On B043 I agree with you that Walter and Mori are a clean pair and that the mechanism is textbook. My difficulty is the one you also record, that the link to human disease is indirect, so I place it behind B020, where human interferonopathies at least show a disease consequence, and behind B004. I would not add it as a second part now because that would require cutting the GLP-1 trio, which I think is the worse trade. That is a judgement about consequence weighting and not a doubt about the science.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius kept B025 (CAR-T) as the strongest fallback if B027 attribution cannot be defended, calling it a clean concept-to-cure chain apart from the Eshhar problem, and argued that clinical benefit with defined credit deserves serious weight.
responses.response: I accept the force of the clinical record, and I agree CAR-T is the most likely fallback if the Committee found B027 too contested. My remaining objection is that the fallback has the same type of attribution problem as the thing it would replace, so it does not remove the risk. Eshhar's chimeric-receptor concept is outside the credited names, and June, Sadelain and Rosenberg represent costimulation, clinical translation and adoptive transfer, which are distinct strands. That is a harder credit puzzle than Mojsov versus Knudsen, where the three core strands are clear. Efficacy so far also rests mainly on haematological cancers. So I would not let the B027 attribution doubts push the Committee to B025 this year; the contested third seat is a reason for careful citation wording, not for switching achievements. I have not moved my alternatives to B025 as a result, but I take your point that it deserves a place on any serious fallback list.

responses.point: Linnarsson argued that the Drucker, Holst and Mojsov trio is the most defensible reading of the discovery, with drug engineering treated as translation, and asked whether a citation covering the physiology only would handle the three-name cap.
responses.response: I agree with that framing and with the answer that the cap is best handled by the citation. The citation I propose names the physiology of GLP-1 and the identity of its active form and then says that this made incretin-based therapy possible, which is accurate and does not leave the Committee claiming that one person made a medicine. Where I would temper your position is the phrase that the trio is the most defensible reading. It is the most defensible reading of the discovery, but it is still a judgement call between discovery and development, and Knudsen's omission will be criticised however carefully we word it. I would not call the choice free of cost. I would rather say plainly that we are making it, and that the alternative reading would have a defensible trio too.

responses.point: El-Manira stated that he would not object to Knudsen if the Committee found the priority questions unresolvable, and framed the issue as physiology and peptide identity against pharmaceutical optimisation.
responses.response: I share that framing, and I think your willingness to move is the right position in principle, but I would set the threshold high. A priority dispute around Mojsov that cannot be settled from the supplied papers is not by itself evidence that her contribution fails; it is a reason for caution. I would change the third seat only if the Committee obtained evidence that the active-peptide identification is not separable from work outside the credited list, and then I would ask first whether Habener belongs in the discussion before Knudsen does. Replacing Mojsov with Knudsen without that evidence would turn a physiology prize into a development prize on the strength of an unresolved doubt, and I would not support that.

uncertainties: Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1 peptide relative to Habener's group is not settled by the supplied material and I rely on recalled history; if evidence showed her contribution is not separable, the third seat would need reconsideration, and I would examine Habener before Knudsen.

Whether any citation wording can avoid reading as a choice between physiology and drug development; I think wording that says the discovery made the therapies possible is the best available, but the exclusion of Knudsen will be criticised either way.

If B027 were set aside, I have not settled the fallback between B020 (clean two-person credit but no delivered therapy), B004 (clear disease link but contested autoimmune etiology and a multi-group priority question) and B025 (strong clinical record but the Eshhar attribution problem); this does not change my preferred configuration.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any shortlisted candidate or credited name. My nuclear-receptor work with Ronald Evans and my collaboration with Johan Ericson are not connected to any shortlisted ballot. I have about twenty co-authored works with Per Svenningsson and one with Abdel El Manira, which I disclose as context; I do not regard it as requiring recusal, and I have tried to test the chair's arguments on their merits rather than defer to him. As Secretary I have no information on any private deliberations beyond this simulation.
